data.connection_issues: Repair issue when a source is unreachable

data_description.scan_interval: Seconds between polls of the inverter.
data_description.power_control: Expose the SunSpec active power limit as a number and a switch. The datalogger accepts the writes on every inverter, but only some inverters act on them; verify with the test described in the documentation before relying on it.
data_description.connection_issues: Raise a repair issue when Modbus or the datalogger REST API keeps failing while the sun is up. Failures at night are ignored: a sleeping inverter is not a fault.
data_description.failures_threshold: Consecutive failed polls in daylight before the issue is raised. Polls slow down to every 5 minutes after the third failure.
data_description.notify_recovery: Post a persistent notification when a source answers again after an issue was raised.
data_description.recovery_script: A script to run once when the issue is raised, for example one that power-cycles the datalogger through a smart plug.

read_registers.name: Read registers
read_registers.description: Reads registers at an absolute Modbus address and decodes them. Returns the raw registers and the decoded value.

count.name: Count
count.description: How many registers to read; ignored for the fixed-size data types.

data_type.name: Data type
data_type.description: How to decode the registers; raw returns them undecoded.

word_order.name: Word order
word_order.description: Which register holds the high word of a 32-bit value.

write_registers.name: Write registers
write_registers.description: Writes one value encoded as the given type, or a list of raw registers, at an absolute Modbus address.

value.name: Value
value.description: The value to encode and write.

values.name: Raw registers
values.description: A list of 16-bit register values to write as they are, instead of a value.

word_order.name: Word order
word_order.description: Which register gets the high word of a 32-bit value.

count.name: Length
count.description: Registers a string spans; defaults to what the string needs.

write_point.name: Write point
write_point.description: Writes a writable SunSpec point by its name, for example WMaxLimPct or OutPFSet, and refreshes the readings.

value.name: Value
value.description: The value in the point's engineering unit.

set_power_limit.name: Set power limit
set_power_limit.description: Sets the active power limit and whether it is applied, verified by reading back. Leave a field out to keep its current value.

percent.name: Limit
percent.description: The limit as a percentage of the rated power.

get_readings.name: Get readings
get_readings.description: Returns every point each device of the entry currently reports.

device.name: Device
device.description: Only this device, by its serial number or identifier.

rediscover.name: Rediscover
rediscover.description: Walks the SunSpec model chain and the datalogger's devices again without reloading, and refreshes the readings. Devices the datalogger reports for the first time get their entities.

connection_failed_modbus.title: {title}: no Modbus answer
connection_failed_modbus.description:
Home Assistant has not been able to read {title} over Modbus TCP at {host} for {failures} consecutive polls during daylight.

Last error: `{error}`

**Possible causes**
- The inverter or its datalogger is powered off or has lost the network
- The address of the device changed
- Another Modbus client has taken over the datalogger, which serves one connection at a time
- The SunSpec settings (unit ID, base address) changed after a firmware update

**What to check**
1. Open the datalogger's web page at http://{host}
2. Look up the device's current address in your router's DHCP table
3. If the address changed, use **Reconfigure** on the integration page

This issue clears by itself as soon as a poll succeeds.

connection_failed_rest.title: {title}: datalogger REST API not answering
connection_failed_rest.description:
Home Assistant has not been able to read the VSN datalogger of {title} at {host} for {failures} consecutive polls during daylight.

Last error: `{error}`

**Possible causes**
- The datalogger is powered off or has lost the network
- The address of the datalogger changed
- The card is stuck; a VSN300 sometimes needs a power cycle after losing its WiFi link

**What to check**
1. Open the datalogger's web page at http://{host}
2. Look up its current address in your router's DHCP table
3. If the address changed, use **Reconfigure** on the integration page
4. Power-cycle the card if the page does not load

This issue clears by itself as soon as a poll succeeds.

unsupported_firmware.title: {title}: datalogger firmware {firmware_version} is not supported
unsupported_firmware.description:
The VSN300 datalogger of {title} at {host} runs firmware {firmware_version}. That release has a known bug: its live data API drops every connection, so nothing can be read from it.

**Please upgrade the datalogger to firmware 2.0.1 or later. The upgrade is mandatory: the integration cannot work with 2.0.0.** It is available from the card's own web page:

1. Open http://{host} and go to the **FW UPDATE** tab
2. Under **Remote Update** click **Check for FW update**; it should offer 2.0.1 or later
3. Click **Download & Update** and wait for the card to update and reboot
4. Reload the integration from its page under Settings > Devices & services

If no update is offered, contact FIMER support. This issue clears by itself once the integration starts.

datalogger_silent.title: {title}: datalogger not reporting on itself
datalogger_silent.description:
The VSN datalogger of {title} at {host} answers and delivers inverter readings, but its own readings (uptime, WiFi link, memory) have been missing for more than {minutes} minutes. The datalogger's sensors stay unavailable until they return.

**Most likely cause**
After a reboot the card could not set its clock (no NTP or internet access) and stopped publishing its own data. This is a known VSN300 firmware quirk.

**What to do**
- Check that the card reaches the internet, for example from its web page at http://{host}
- Power-cycle the card

This issue clears by itself as soon as the card reports on itself again.

confirm.title: Forget the missing devices
confirm.description:
The datalogger of {title} at {host} reported these devices before but does not report them now:

{missing_devices}

Their entities are unavailable meanwhile. Possible causes: the device is off (an inverter at night), disconnected from the datalogger, or removed from the plant. The issue clears by itself once every device is reported again.

Submit only if the devices are gone for good: they and their entities are removed from Home Assistant. A device the datalogger reports again later is added back as new.

takeover_incomplete.title: {title}: {count} legacy sensors were not carried over

confirm.title: Acknowledge
confirm.description:
The entry of the earlier ABB/FIMER PVI VSN REST integration was removed and its sensors were re-registered here, except these, which have no counterpart in this integration:

{entities}

Their history stays in the recorder under the old entity IDs but no entity provides them any more. If you used them in automations or dashboards, point those at the entities of this integration.

Submit to dismiss this notice; the listed sensors are not restored.
